Chapter 16

Automatic drumming pattern timing and recovery

Automatic drumming is the percussion panel within Keirzo control. It has its own Start drumming and Stop buttons. Start robot prepares the arms, lights and selected movement; it does not start hits. The panel can also prepare the required arm connection when Start drumming is pressed. All four arms must pass preparation, even when you intend to play only selected parts.

  1. Choose Music mixer · track beat or Synth mixer · rhythm and notes. This Follow selection stays in sync with the main Keirzo control selector.
  2. Enable the desired kick, ride, snare and hi-hat arms. Choose Straight, Broken beat or Half-time.
  3. Adjust Density, Synth influence where applicable, and Fills. Fills introduce variation every fourth bar.
  4. Press Start drumming. If the selected source is stopped, the panel waits. Start that source’s playback and watch preparation/ready status before expecting hits.
  5. Use the drum panel Stop for drums only, or the top Stop to end all robot performances. Editing a drum setting stops drumming; review the settings and press Start drumming again when ready.

What the drum source actually follows

Music mixer supplies the playing track’s BPM and beat position. Its grid is estimated from requested generation BPM and track start; it is not a detected acoustic beat grid. Synth mixer uses actual note events, including probability, rests, chords and repeats, and the preceding bar’s accents shape the next drum bar. A chord counts as one onset. Synth influence moves from a steadier groove toward those accents. Neither source analyses microphone sound.

Each individual drum is limited to one hit per second, including high-density settings and fills. Different drums may strike together; there is no global spacing interval between different arms. The browser thins the requested pattern and the server independently enforces the same per-arm limit. Expired, duplicated and physically infeasible hits are dropped instead of accumulated.

Rest confirmation and fault handling

When required, startup enables arm torque and moves all four arms to rest over two seconds. Selected arms then receive the normal 500 ms preparation. Each must be inside its strike range and within 20 ticks of rest before a hit is allowed. Nominal profile time is not taken as proof of arrival: a healthy arm gets up to one additional second to settle, with position and health checks every 50 ms or when the bus is available.

A healthy powered arm found outside its playing range has queued hits removed and returns to rest over two seconds. Boundary rest targets are inset by 10 ticks for tolerance, including hi-hat at 2590. It rejoins future hits only after an in-range rest readback. A settling timeout, lost torque or motor fault pauses that arm and retains the reason; other healthy arms can continue. Resolve the reported cause and start a new session for the paused arm. Uncertain movement writes are not automatically retried.

Source stops, track changes and timing discontinuities cancel queued hits. While Start remains active, valid playback can prepare and rejoin automatically. Fast playback-rate changes suspend drumming until the clock settles; synth tempo changes may also need resynchronisation. An adapter disconnect, explicit torque release or emergency stop ends the whole drumming session and requires a new explicit Start. Resetting emergency stop never resumes it.

Timing and diagnostic limits

The browser refreshes a short server queue with a one-second heartbeat timeout. Hits are submitted 650-950 ms before their intended contact. Each arm uses an absolute target contact time: kick, ride and snare start their 150 ms strike profiles before it, and hi-hat starts 200 ms before it. Return profiles are 150 ms. The controller checks/stages the arm before timed dispatch; late or cancelled goals are dropped. A normal stop lets healthy in-flight strokes return, while release, disconnect and emergency stop cancel further motion.

The original Max patch aligned contact by delaying 400 minus the stored hit time, then striking for that time. This implementation schedules directly from the desired contact time and does not add another 400 ms. These are intended profile timings, not measurements of acoustic contact. Dispatched-strike and skipped-hit counts aid diagnosis, but physical contact alignment and continuous multi-arm operation remain to be checked on Keirzo. Keep the selected groove, tempo, affected arm, status reason and observed motion when reporting a failure.

Chapter 17

Native Hydrasynth MIDI Linux audio and older routes

Choose the MIDI path intentionally

The browser Synth mixer can send through Web MIDI independently of the native controller. make dashboard-sonify is enough for browser sound and, with browser MIDI permission, browser-driven Hydrasynth output. make dashboard starts the native hydractl service for hardware telemetry and the local command broker. The native service and browser output have separate connection behavior; selecting one does not turn USB MIDI into an audio interface.

  1. Connect and power the synth, start with monitor volume low, and connect its analogue output to headphones, speakers or an audio interface. Hydrasynth USB carries MIDI commands, not the synth’s audio.
  2. On the synth, match MIDI RX to the intended channel. Browser output uses channel 1; native commands default to 1 but accept --channel 1-16. For the documented acceptance rig, MPE is off.
  3. Use PARAM RX=NRPN for dashboard catalog mappings. Named native timbre commands use CC and need PARAM RX=CC. Choose PARAM TX=CC or NRPN according to the feedback you want to observe. Enable PGM CHG RX for remote patch changes and PGM CHG TX for front-panel patch tracking.
  4. List native endpoints, then launch the live dashboard if you need its telemetry/broker. Stop an existing dashboard before launching another on port 8790. Inspect the selected destination and source before sending a note.
./build/hydractl list
aconnect -l
make dashboard

A native destination can be selected with --device using a unique name or Linux ALSA client:port address. Numeric addresses can change after reconnecting or rebooting. Prefer a unique name for a saved launch command; ambiguous matches fail. To pass native options through Make, for example, use make dashboard DASHBOARD_ARGS='--device "unique device name" --channel 1'. Replace the example with the listed name.

The native service detects MIDI loss, stops scheduling and exits. Reconnect the intended synth and restart the live dashboard/service; there is no native automatic reconnection. The browser Web MIDI path can rediscover its saved device, but requires Play again after disconnection. Physical USB removal can prevent delivery of note-off messages, so inspect the instrument for held notes when recovering.

Native command reference

Run these sending examples only after selecting the intended synth and establishing a listening level. Patch selection discards unsaved edits in the current synth buffer. The following are independent terminal commands; while the live dashboard owns a service, use its command client for shared scheduled operations rather than accidentally starting a second service.

CommandPurpose
./build/hydractl note C4 --velocity 72 --duration 0.5One bounded note; note names or MIDI numbers are accepted.
./build/hydractl sequence C4 E4 G4 C5 --step 0.2 --gate 0.7A short note sequence; step is seconds and gate is 0-1.
./build/hydractl timbre listList the named normalized CC controls.
./build/hydractl timbre cutoff 0.70Set a named value from 0-1 with PARAM RX=CC.
./build/hydractl cc 74 96Send a raw CC number/value from 0-127.
./build/hydractl nrpn 1234 8192Raw NRPN example; address/value are 0-16383. Select a documented parameter before use.
./build/hydractl patch A 1Select bank A, patch 1; patch numbers are 1-128.
./build/hydractl bend -0.5Normalized pitch bend from -1 to +1; return to 0 afterwards.
.venv/bin/python -B tools/hydra_command.py --pretty '{
  "v":1, "id":"state-1", "op":"state"
}'

.venv/bin/python -B tools/hydra_command.py '{
  "v":1, "id":"short-note", "op":"play",
  "notes":[60], "velocity":72, "duration_ms":500
}'

The client talks to the live dashboard’s private local Unix socket and reads its generated token automatically. Demo mode has no native command broker. Each request carries an ID so the response can be matched. Scheduled play supplies its own note-offs; direct note_on clients must provide note_off. The service also supports overlapping scheduled notes and linear CC ramps, state/status queries, job cancellation and user takeover protection. A physical control movement normally blocks competing non-forced writes to that parameter for three seconds. The technical reference in docs/reference.md documents the full NDJSON protocol.

Current native cleanup caveat: hydractl panic sends CC64, CC123 and CC120. The persistent service’s panic, shutdown and failed-note-off cleanup also send CC120, with service-wide panic covering all 16 channels. The repository’s Hydrasynth mapping assigns CC120 to ARP Octave, so do not treat native panic as a transparent routine reset that preserves the patch’s arpeggiator settings. Browser All notes off uses sustain-off and All Notes Off without CC120. This existing native/documentation discrepancy needs hardware validation; retain the synth state when investigating it. MIDI cleanup is separate from Keirzo Emergency stop.

Audio capture and level checks on Linux

./build/hydra-audio list --json
./build/hydra-audio meter --device 'Revolution 2x2' --channel 1 --duration 2 --json
# Or replace this UID with the actual UID in your list:
./build/hydra-audio meter --uid 'hw:CARD=USB,DEV=0' --channel 1 --duration 2 --json

hydra-audio is an input meter. It neither records an audio file nor supplies native synthesis/playback; the dashboard plays through the browser. The default selection is a device containing Revolution 2x2, channel 1, for ten seconds. Explicit durations are 0.1-3600 seconds. Channels are one-based. --device selects by name; --uid selects the listed ALSA PCM identifier and can disambiguate a device. A card-name UID is more stable than a numeric card index.

Play a known signal into the selected interface input and inspect frames, elapsed time, RMS, peak, clipping and non-finite counts. Clipping means a sample at or above an absolute value of 1.0, or 0 dBFS; use the interface/synth gain controls to resolve an excessive input level. Healthy physical acceptance requires plausible nonzero capture duration and counts, finite values, a signal above idle noise and no clipping at the intended level. A synthetic passing test cannot verify the physical cable, input channel or gain.

Direct hw: capture can be busy when another program owns the interface. Close the conflicting capture application or select --uid default or an explicitly configured PipeWire/PulseAudio ALSA PCM. No change of system audio server is required. Desktop/custom route listing intentionally reports zero channels/rate when capability is unknown, without opening that backend. Selection and metering determine the usable format. arecord -l lists capture hardware; /dev/snd/seq access is needed for native MIDI, including in containers.

Earlier interfaces and legacy integration

The Previous version link in Synth mixer opens #synth-legacy, retaining its older per-recording mapping tabs and presets. The older movement-driven electronic drum interface remains at #drums and uses a six-voice browser kit; it is distinct from Keirzo’s four physical arms. Observer is at /observer/ and can display native/demo telemetry or the Signal Lab feed. These views share the dashboard, but their output and source choices still matter.

The direct Keirzo motor controls do not require the sibling drumming-robot repository, Max or interaction.py at runtime. Their ranges and strike timing were derived from those older files; do not launch the old serial bridge alongside the dashboard merely because the manual mentions that provenance. After connecting real hardware on Linux, complete docs/hardware_acceptance.md for MIDI feedback, notes, scheduling, disconnects and audio, and perform the robot checks in docs/robot_control.md. Record the machine, build, device firmware, exact command/settings and physical result.

Chapter 18

Daily operation updates and saved material

A consistent start and finish

  1. Start the server from the correct checkout using the same study-directory override, if any, that you used previously. Read the startup lines showing its study and backup locations.
  2. Open the usual local browser address. Check the desired input and output in Connections before playback. Reconnecting a device and selecting a saved session do not by themselves resume playback.
  3. Before participant work, open the researcher view and confirm storage health, the intended laptop ID and participant session. Keep the machine on reliable power and check available storage.
  4. At the end, stop audio and robot activities, let pending study records reach Saved locally, and then stop the foreground server with Ctrl+C. Collect the completed backups as described below.

Update an existing laptop

git status --short
git pull --ff-only && bash tools/setup.sh
make dashboard-sonify

Stop the running dashboard before updating. Review git status first: local source edits need to be preserved or reconciled, not discarded. The fast-forward pull refuses an unexpected history merge rather than guessing how to combine it. Rerun setup after pulling to update Python dependencies within the supported versions and rebuild native tools. Whisper is installed automatically if missing. It preserves the existing usable environment, model, key and local data. A failure during an update is a reason to resolve the reported problem before beginning a participant session.

All six laptops should use the same application revision during a study. A clone or pull receives only committed, pushed files. It does not carry an uncommitted local fix, .env, .venv, generated media or the normal study folder. Record the revision with git rev-parse HEAD when checking a prepared machine.

Know what is saved where

MaterialLocation and transfer rule
Application and bundled assetsGit checkout. Update through Git. The bundled recordings are compressed and read directly.
API credential.env in this checkout. Keep private; provision separately on each laptop.
Speech modelvar/whisper/small. May be copied to save downloads.
Generated music and rap assetsProject var folders, including var/elevenlabs and var/rap-response. Saved session audio snapshots normally live in var/session-assets. Export Sessions ZIPs to transfer the audio referenced by saved versions; preserve the service folders when migrating the complete generated library.
Mixer settings and Sessions librarySettings and named versions use this browser’s local storage. Export selected/all sessions as ZIP, including their generated audio, before changing browser, profile or origin.
Study journal and microphone mediaThe configured study-data directory. Independent of the Sessions settings library.
Head calibrationvar/robot/head-calibration.json. Local and specific to the physical robot.

Sessions ZIP exports carry settings and their referenced completed generated audio. Opening the ZIP on another prepared laptop restores that audio when a version loads. Older Sessions JSON files contain references only and require the original audio to remain available. Study export bundles serve an analysis/archive purpose and are not an automatic import mechanism for the application’s music library.

Use the same browser address consistently: http://127.0.0.1:8790 and http://localhost:8790 have different browser origins, as does a different port. Their local settings and permissions can therefore differ even though they reach the same server. Clearing site data, using another browser profile or opening a private window can make saved settings appear to have disappeared.

Chapter 19

Study recording and participant handovers

Study recording and local backup creation are enabled automatically. Participants do not have to press Record for ordinary interaction logging or perform a save/export step. Explicit microphone recording remains an intentional user action. Researcher controls are shown at http://127.0.0.1:8790/?researcher=1. This query option changes the presentation and is not an authentication mechanism.

Create a handover in the participant’s own tab

  1. In the same browser tab the participant will use, open the address with ?researcher=1 and expand Study.
  2. Enter an optional participant code and choose New participant. Confirm the displayed session before continuing.
  3. Remove the researcher query option to return to the ordinary participant view. Keep using this tab.
  4. At the next handover, repeat the procedure in that same tab. A second researcher tab has its own session and cannot mark a handover in the participant tab.

Without an explicit handover, the recorder sees a continuous session and cannot infer that somebody else has started. A page reload preserves the tab’s session while creating a new client run. Activity without a participant code is still recorded. These participant sessions are different from the header’s Sessions library, which stores mixer/settings snapshots.

What the records describe

The recorder captures interface actions, accepted mapping configurations, playback and output events, browser/backend errors, numeric live input, generation settings and job transitions. Microphone clips include original recordings and relevant transcription submissions; transcripts, supplied words, generated lyrics and audio references are retained. Mapping configuration and playback revision IDs help relate a setup to the period when it was used. Canceled microphone attempts are also retained when study recording is enabled; canceling a rap is not deletion of the study capture.

Events include device, participant-session and client identifiers, timestamps, elapsed time, sequence information and application revision. Some backend hardware events have no known participant and remain unassigned; they can be aligned by laptop and time. A command or scheduled output record does not prove that a speaker sounded or a robot physically made contact. Recording does not add continuous ambient microphone, screen or camera capture.

Storage and health

On Linux the default is $XDG_DATA_HOME/keirzo/study-data, or ~/.local/share/keirzo/study-data when XDG_DATA_HOME is unset. macOS uses ~/Library/Application Support/Keirzo/study-data. KEIRZO_STUDY_DIR or --study-dir chooses another local directory. The development machine may have been started with var/study-data explicitly; use the actual startup message and Study backup path rather than assuming a location.

Each fresh study database creates its own installation ID. Do not copy the database between operational laptops. Keep live databases on local storage rather than inside a cloud-synchronised folder. Browser IndexedDB queues events and completed clips until the backend acknowledges them; the backend persists the journal in SQLite with separate audio files. This works without internet access, but it still needs the local server and writable disk.

Watch for pending recordings and storage errors in Study. Keep the tab open while work is pending, and resolve a full disk or denied folder access before closing. An abrupt browser/process exit can lose an unfinished microphone recording or events that have not reached persistent storage. The system does not automatically delete old sessions or recordings, so plan disk space and retention for the study.

For development, --no-study-recording disables recording entirely. --no-study-backups disables only the automatic backup bundles; it leaves primary recording enabled. Do not add either flag to participant launch commands by habit. Keep laptop clocks synchronised before a session; timestamp alignment cannot repair unknown clock drift after the fact.

Back to contents

Chapter 20

Collecting exporting and combining study data

Automatic backups are incremental

Automatic backups run at server startup, every two minutes and during normal shutdown. Completed ZIP files appear under study-data/backups/<laptop-id>/. Each adds new events, microphone clips and new or changed generated audio. Retain every ZIP in that folder: the newest file is not a complete substitute for the earlier files. Failed backups are retried while primary local recording continues.

These automatic copies remain on the same laptop until you copy them to another device. They do not protect against loss of the entire laptop on their own. There is no automatic upload. Data still pending in the browser becomes eligible for backup only after the backend has saved it. These ZIPs can contain participant transcripts and microphone audio. The application does not encrypt the archives; handle collection drives as participant data.

Collect onto USB after a session

  1. Open the researcher Study panel in the participant tab. Stop the activity and wait until pending recordings have drained and the status reports Saved locally.
  2. Check Backups for a recent successful write and no error. Saved locally confirms primary storage, not ZIP backup success. If backups fail, use Export this laptop while the server is still running and verify that archive. A clean shutdown alone does not prove the final backup succeeded.
  3. Stop the server normally with Ctrl+C and allow the final backup to finish. Do not force-kill the process just to speed up collection.
  4. Locate the backups folder shown by the server/Study panel and copy the entire backups folder to your collection drive. Preserve every per-laptop subfolder and completed ZIP.
  5. Repeat for each laptop. Check that the expected six installation folders and files are present on the collection drive before removing it.
  6. Keep the originals until the collected files have been verified and the study’s retention process says they can be removed.

A complete manual snapshot

With the server running and the browser queue drained, choose Study > Export this laptop. This downloads a separate complete snapshot of all recorded sessions on this installation, leaving the originals intact. It does not reset automatic backup progress. The archive contains exact JSONL, analysis-friendly CSV, participant-session records, linked audio, job metadata and a manifest with file hashes and unavailable-asset details.

A job that is still generating may not yet have completed audio. The manifest reports unavailable assets rather than pretending they exist. Export again after generation has finished if those assets are needed. A manual full export can be collected alongside incremental ZIPs; repeated identical events are deduplicated by the merge tool.

Merge the collection for analysis

.venv/bin/python tools/study_merge.py /path/to/collected-laptops --output /path/to/study-analysis

Run this from an installed checkout on the analysis computer. The input can be a directory containing nested laptop folders or individual ZIP paths. The command discovers complete ZIP bundles recursively and combines them by event ID. Conflicting content under the same event identity is treated as an error rather than silently choosing one version.

The analysis directory includes combined.sqlite3, event/session/media CSV files, exact JSONL and collected audio. media.csv links microphone clips to their participant sessions and local files. Use JSONL for exact nested payloads; CSV escapes formula-like text for spreadsheet use. Exceptionally large browser events may be stored as recording.event_chunk fragments. Reconstruct one logical event by joining its JSON strings in chunk_index order for the matching logical_event_id.

Check the merge result and each manifest’s missing-assets information before treating the collection as complete. Keep collected archives alongside the analysis output so a later script or interpretation can be rerun from the source records. Exporting or merging data does not automatically repopulate a dashboard’s Sessions library or generated-media store.

Chapter 21

Troubleshooting and verification

Start with the visible status message and the terminal running the server. Resolve installation and local browser issues before diagnosing physical equipment. The following checks do not require a robot or synthesizer unless the row explicitly refers to connected hardware.

SymptomAction
The page will not openConfirm the terminal still shows a running dashboard, then open http://127.0.0.1:8790 on that same laptop. If you chose --port, use that number. Check for an immediate startup error.
Address already in use on port 8790Check whether the existing dashboard is the one you want. Stop it from its original terminal before launching another. ss -ltnp can identify a listener; inspect its command and PID before terminating anything.
An old var/dashboard.pid file existsThe normal installer does not manage a background service or PID file. A PID file from a previous manual launcher can be stale. Verify the process and command line before acting; do not blindly kill the number in the file.
Setup says Python has no version setUse bash tools/setup_linux.sh, which selects /usr/bin/python3 for a new environment, or set PYTHON to a real Python 3.10+ executable. For an installed checkout, use .venv/bin/python directly.
The existing .venv is unusableSetup deliberately keeps it intact. Stop the app, move that environment aside, and rerun setup with a suitable interpreter. Do not copy a .venv from another laptop.
The native build cannot find alsa/asoundlib.hInstall libasound2-dev and pkg-config or provide the matching extracted headers described in docs/linux.md. --skip-system does not install these dependencies.
No sound from Test soundCheck system volume, browser/site mute, the selected system output device and headphones. Click Test sound directly to activate browser audio. Test sound always uses browser audio; the separate Synth output setting determines where Synth mixer playback goes.
Playback waits for mapped inputVerify Signals from matches the source you configured. Choose Simulated demo signals for a standalone check, or select a recording/live input in Connections. An enabled mapping with missing input can pause sound.
New generation says the key is missingRun .venv/bin/python tools/configure_api_key.py in a terminal, then restart the dashboard. Ensure it is the .env in this checkout and check whether an environment variable overrides it.
Provider authentication, access or quota errorCheck the key’s expiry/revocation, endpoint permissions, account feature access and available credits in the provider dashboard. Provision a replacement with --replace when necessary. Repeated generation attempts can create additional paid requests.
Microphone recording is unavailableGrant microphone permission for this local browser origin and select an input in the operating system. Installation and model readiness do not grant browser permission. Use typed text while resolving capture.
Transcription says the model is missingRun .venv/bin/python tools/prepare_rap_transcription.py, or copy a complete var/whisper/small folder and rerun setup. The model and Python dependencies are both required.
Whisper will not load on this CPURead the installer’s load error. Confirm a complete model and a compatible installed transcription environment. Typed input is available while the local transcription issue is resolved.
hydractl list cannot open the ALSA sequencerCheck aconnect -l and access to /dev/snd/seq. Run under the ordinary logged-in desktop user with device access. A container may lack sound devices even when the host has them.
MIDI list contains only MIDI ThroughNo Hydrasynth is currently exposed to ALSA. That is expected without the synth connected. Check power, USB and device enumeration once the physical instrument is available.
Native MIDI works but browser MIDI does notThese are separate paths. Grant Web MIDI permission in a browser that supports it and choose the output in Connections. A native connection does not grant browser permission.
A native device disconnectedReconnect the intended device, then stop and restart the native service. It deliberately does not select another instrument. Prefer a unique device name; ALSA numeric client:port addresses can change.
An ALSA audio route lists zero channels/rateNamed desktop/custom routes may have unknown capability metadata until metering starts. Use the actual UID to select the route; zero metadata alone is not proof of failure.
Direct hw: capture is busyAnother client may own the audio device. Close that capture client or select a shared/default PipeWire/PulseAudio ALSA route. The project does not require replacing the desktop audio server.
Robot serial permission deniedCheck the selected serial device and user groups. On Ubuntu, dialout membership is commonly needed; log out/in after an administrator changes it. Do not run the dashboard as root.
Study is pending or reports a storage errorKeep the participant tab open. Check that the local server is running, the study folder is writable and disk space is available. Retry export only after pending data has reached local storage.
Saved settings seem missing after restartCheck browser profile and the exact hostname/port. Named versions are browser-local. Use Sessions > Open file... to restore an exported ZIP with its generated audio. Older JSON files need their referenced audio on the server.

Verification without physical equipment

make native-test
make test

native-test runs both C self-tests and the Linux ALSA integration suite. It uses isolated virtual MIDI peers and synthetic audio rather than choosing a physical instrument or microphone. Tests that need unavailable ALSA sequencer access report a skip; a skipped test is not evidence that the host MIDI path works. make test adds the full Python/JavaScript dashboard suite and requires Node.js and permission to create local sockets.

For a prepared laptop, also verify Test sound, a bundled recording, a simulated signal and a saved voice demo. Confirm the researcher panel shows the expected installation ID and that a completed backup exists. These checks establish the local workflow without spending provider credits. A separate, intentionally initiated provider test is needed to establish generation access.

Physical MIDI reception, note-off/panic, real audio channels and levels, serial device identity, head calibration, emergency stop and robot stroke limits still require the actual rig. Use docs/hardware_acceptance.md and the hardware chapters of this manual when it is connected. Passing synthetic tests does not verify acoustic output or safe movement of an assembled robot.

Chapter 22

Reference glossary and verification

Use this glossary to connect the interface language with the different data, sound and hardware paths. The web application is also called Hydra Signal Lab; hydractl and hydra-audio are its separate native command-line tools.

TermMeaning in this project
Recording inputBundled or externally selected RAPP movement data. It is data used to drive mappings, not an audio recording of the synth.
Signal mixA named normalized control signal built from one or more input fields. A mix must be assigned to a destination before it changes that sound parameter.
Manual valueThe base setting of a parameter. Signal strength blends between this value and the mapped signal.
StemOne separated component of a generated music track, such as bass or drums. Stem availability depends on successful preparation.
Browser audioSound generated or played by the browser through the computer output device. It needs a user gesture to start and is independent of native MIDI.
Web MIDIBrowser access to MIDI devices. Permission, saved-device selection and browser compatibility are separate from ALSA access in the native service.
ALSALinux audio and MIDI interfaces used by the native controller and input meter. Native MIDI uses the sequencer; the meter uses PCM input.
CC and NRPNMIDI control encodings. Match the synth reception setting to the command type; a received controller number does not have the same meaning on every instrument.
TorqueThe motor holding/driving force. Stopping a pattern, disconnecting a port and releasing torque are distinct actions.
Session versionA named snapshot of application settings with referenced completed generated audio. Exported ZIPs include that audio; movement recordings and participant study records remain separate.
Study sessionRecorded interaction events and linked media for one participant/session on a laptop. This is separate from the Sessions settings library.
Incremental backupAn archive of new events and new/changed media since previous backups. Retain the whole backup sequence.
Localhost127.0.0.1 refers to the computer on which the browser is running. Six laptops each run their own server and store their own data.

How this edition was checked

The instructions were checked against the local README, Linux setup guide, robot control guide, hardware acceptance checklist, command-line help and current dashboard implementation on 20 October 2026. Screenshots were captured from the running application. Robot and synth hardware were absent; provider generation was not exercised.

The Linux native implementation previously passed both C self-tests and all 21 virtual MIDI/synthetic audio integration cases without skips. The dashboard suite passed 692 Python cases plus JavaScript behavior/syntax checks. Installer follow-up checks passed 14 credential-helper cases and 33 provider-service cases; the actual repeat-install path and offline model load passed. A first installation on a clean laptop, physical operation and provider account access remain separate acceptance checks.

Known native MIDI limitation: the current native panic/shutdown cleanup sends CC120, which the Hydrasynth mapping uses for ARP Octave. Review the native MIDI chapter before relying on cleanup behavior with a physical instrument. The browser All notes off path is different.

Maintaining this manual

The repository contains docs/manual-content.json, original screenshots in docs/manual-assets, the offline HTML/PDF outputs and tools/build_manual.py. Regenerate after changing source material or replacing screenshots. HTML generation requires only Python; PDF generation additionally requires ReportLab and DejaVu fonts. On Ubuntu/Debian, fonts-dejavu-core supplies those fonts.

# HTML only, using the application environment:
.venv/bin/python tools/build_manual.py --html-only

# Optional PDF authoring dependencies and complete rebuild:
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-manual.txt
.venv/bin/python tools/build_manual.py

Supporting repository documents: README.md; docs/reference.md; docs/linux.md; docs/macos.md; docs/robot_control.md; docs/hardware_acceptance.md; docs/live_streaming.md; docs/movement_drums.md. Provider key permissions and quotas can change; check the current official documentation at https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/workspaces/api-keys.
